title: TotalEnergies, TES, Osaka Gas, Toho Gas and ITOCHU Partner Up to Develop the Live Oak Project for e-NG Production in Nebraska
summary: Paris, December 2, 2025 – TotalEnergies, TES, Osaka Gas, Toho Gas, and ITOCHU have signed a Joint Development and Operating Agreement, granting the Japanese companies a combined 33.3% stake in the Live Oak project — a large-scale facility to produce electric natural gas (e-NG) also known as e-methane, initiated by TotalEnergies and TES and currently under […]
body_text: Paris, December 2, 2025 – TotalEnergies, TES, Osaka Gas, Toho Gas, and ITOCHU have signed a Joint Development and Operating Agreement, granting the Japanese companies a combined 33.3% stake in the Live Oak project — a large-scale facility to produce electric natural gas (e-NG) also known as e-methane, initiated by TotalEnergies and TES and currently under development in Nebraska, United States. Following the agreement, TotalEnergies and TES will each maintain a 33.35 % stake in the project. The partners are now preparing the Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) phase, targeting a capacity of approximately 250 MW of electrolysis and 75 ktpa of methanation. The project, subject to a Final Investment Decision in 2027, is scheduled to begin commercial operations by 2030, with plans to export e-NG to Japan. Osaka Gas and Toho Gas will be the primary offtakers. This project helps the Japanese gas majors in achieving their goal of injecting 1% carbon neutral gas (such as e-NG) into the gas grid by 2030. The agreement builds on the strategic partnership established between TotalEnergies and TES in 2023 to pioneer at scale production of e-NG. The Live Oak project will leverage Nebraska's abundant biogenic CO₂ resources, captured from bioethanol plants, and the growing renewable power generation capacity in the United States. The participation of Osaka Gas, Toho Gas, and ITOCHU (as a coordinator of Japanese companies), underscores their commitment to decarbonization with the adoption of e-NG and positions Live Oak as the leading project for carbon-neutral gas production for Japan. e-NG is a synthetic gas produced from renewable hydrogen and CO₂. Chemically identical to conventional natural gas, e-NG can be seamlessly integrated into existing LNG infrastructure—liquefaction, transport, regasification, and distribution—without any alterations to consumer equipment.

title: Inside Sales vs Outside Sales
summary: Tired of the inside vs. outside sales debate? It's outdated. Get our pragmatic guide to structuring a modern sales team & learn how AI is the real winner.
body_text: Inside Sales vs Outside Sales: The 5-Second Comparison For the scanners and the skeptics, let's cut to the chase. Here’s the high-level breakdown. No fluff, just the facts. Factor Inside Sales Outside Sales Work Environment Office or remote desk. High-energy, collaborative, and digitally native. On the road. Autonomous, face-to-face, and geographically focused. Sales Cycle Short to medium (days to weeks). Higher velocity, more transactional. Long to very long (months to years). Complex, relationship-driven. Deal Size Typically smaller to mid-sized deals (lower ACV). Typically larger, high-value enterprise deals (higher ACV). Key Tools CRM, dialers, sales engagement platforms, video conferencing, AI SDRs. CRM (mobile), mapping software, expense tracking, travel apps. Core Skill Efficiency and tech-savviness. Juggling a high volume of leads. Relationship building and strategic negotiation. Navigating complex organizations. Best For… SaaS, tech, and businesses with a transactional or high-velocity sales model. Manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and businesses with complex, high-ticket products. What is Inside Sales? (Hint: It’s Not Just "Sales From an Office") Inside sales, or remote sales, is a model where reps sell products and services from a distance. They connect with prospects using phones, email, video calls, and social media. Think of them as digital-first sales athletes, running plays from a central hub. This isn't your parents' telemarketing. Modern inside sales is sophisticated, data-driven, and relies heavily on a finely tuned tech stack to engage prospects at scale. It’s less about cold calling down a list and more about creating a high-velocity pipeline through smart, targeted outreach. A Day in the Life of an Inside Sales Rep An inside sales rep's day is a masterclass in time management. It's a high-volume, high-energy environment powered by caffeine and closing tabs. The morning might be dedicated to a block of outbound calls and personalized emails. The afternoon is packed with back-to-back product demos over video conference, followed by updating the CRM with meticulous notes. It’s a rhythm of outreach, engagement, qualification, and closing—all without ever leaving their desk. The Inside Sales Tech Stack The inside sales rep’s toolkit is their lifeline. Without the right tech, they’re flying blind. The essentials include: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) : The single source of truth for all lead and customer data (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce) Sales Engagement Platforms : Tools to automate email sequences and manage multi-channel outreach Auto-Dialers : For maximizing call volume and efficiency Video Conferencing : The modern substitute for the in-person handshake AI Prospecting Tools : The unfair advantage. AI SDRs like Topo automate the entire top of the funnel—from finding intent signals to enriching data and launching outreach—so reps can focus on qualified conversations What is Outside Sales? (AKA Field Sales, for the Old-School Crowd) Outside sales, or field sales, is the traditional model where reps meet prospects face-to-face. These are the road warriors who build relationships over handshakes, client lunches, and conference floor demos. Their territory isn't a CRM dashboard; it's a geographical map. This model is built on the power of human connection. It’s best suited for complex, high-ticket sales where trust and in-person validation are critical to closing the deal. While technology has changed the game, the core of outside sales remains the same: being physically present to navigate complex deals and build lasting partnerships. A Day in the Life of an Outside Sales Rep Forget the 9-to-5 desk grind. An outside sales rep's day is defined by movement. It starts with a drive or flight to a client's city. The day is structured around a few key meetings: a presentation at a prospect's headquarters, a strategic lunch with a key decision-maker, and maybe a networking event in the evening. In between, they’re on their phone, updating the CRM, and filing expense reports for that “strategic lunch.” It’s a life of autonomy, travel, and mastering the art of the expense account. The Outside Sales Tech Stack Even road warriors need a digital toolkit. Their tech is all about mobile productivity: Mobile CRM : Accessing and updating lead information on the go is non-negotiable Mapping Software : For planning efficient routes between client meetings Expense Tracking Apps : To turn that pile of receipts into a clean report without losing your mind Productivity Apps : Note-taking, document scanning, and presentation tools that work offline Key Differences That Actually Matter Okay, you get the basics. One is at a desk, one is in a car. But the real difference between inside sales and outside sales impacts your strategy, budget, and team structure. Let's dig in. Sales Cycle & Deal Complexity This is the big one. Inside sales thrives on speed. With shorter sales cycles (often under 90 days), the goal is to move a high volume of transactional deals through the pipeline. The product is typically easier to understand and buy without a dozen stakeholder meetings. Outside sales plays the long game. Sales cycles can stretch from six months to over a year, involving complex products, multi-million dollar contracts, and navigating a labyrinth of decision-makers. It’s less about velocity and more about strategic, patient cultivation of a few massive opportunities. Cost & Scalability Let’s talk money. The cost of an outside sales team is significantly higher. A study by Spotio found that an outside sales call costs an average of $308, while an inside sales call costs just $50. Why? Travel, accommodations, meals, and entertainment—it all adds up. Because of this, inside sales teams are far more cost-effective and easier to scale. You can hire five inside sales reps for the cost of one or two field reps, allowing you to cover more ground, faster. Relationship Building Here’s a myth we need to bust: that only outside sales reps can build real relationships. It’s an old-school take that just doesn’t hold up anymore. A handshake is great, but so is a well-timed, insightful email followed by a crisp video call where you share your screen and solve a problem in real time. Modern inside sales reps build rapport through consistency, expertise, and digital savvy. They use video to create face-to-face connections and social media to stay top-of-mind. The relationship isn't weaker; it's just built through a different medium. Which Model is Right for Your Business? (Stop Guessing) Choosing between inside sales vs outside sales isn't a coin flip. It’s a strategic decision based on your product, market, and customer. If you’re a Head of Sales trying to build a winning team, stop guessing and use this framework. Decision Checklist Run your business through this checklist. The more you check on the left, the more you lean inside. The more on the right, the more you lean outside. Product Price & Complexity : Is your average contract value (ACV) under $100k and easy to demonstrate remotely? Lean inside . Is it a complex, seven-figure deal that requires on-site integration? Lean outside . Customer Location : Are your customers spread out nationally or globally? An inside team is the only way to scale cost-effectively. Are they concentrated in a few key cities or industrial parks? Outside reps can work that territory effectively. Sales Process : Is your sales motion fast, repeatable, and transactional? That’s a perfect fit for an inside sales engine. Does it involve lengthy pilots, multiple C-level presentations, and on-site proof-of-concepts? You’ll need an outside team. Market Maturity : Are you selling a new, disruptive product that requires a lot of education? An inside team can run high-volume educational plays. Are you in a mature industry built on long-standing relationships? An outside rep with a good reputation is invaluable. Industry-Specific Examples SaaS : The classic inside sales model. Most SaaS companies use inside SDRs to generate leads and inside AEs to demo and close, especially for SMB and mid-market deals. They may add a small team of enterprise field reps for the whale accounts. For a deeper breakdown of these roles, see BDR vs SDR vs AE . Manufacturing : Traditionally the domain of outside sales . Reps visit plants, build relationships with distributors, and sell heavy machinery. However, many are now adopting a hybrid approach, using inside sales teams to handle smaller accounts or generate leads for their field reps. Professional Services : Almost always a hybrid model. An inside sales team might qualify leads and book initial discovery calls. But closing a six-figure consulting project requires an outside partner to be in the room, reading the body language and building C-level trust. The Rise of Hybrid and AI-Driven Sales Teams You’ve probably noticed a theme here. The smartest companies aren't choosing one or the other. They're asking a better question: "How can we combine the scalability of inside sales with the high-touch impact of outside sales?" The answer is a hybrid sales model, supercharged by AI. This isn't a compromise; it's the next evolution. The "vs." in inside sales vs outside sales is officially dead. Welcome to the era of the unified, intelligent sales engine. How AI is Blurring the Lines The real enemy of any sales team isn’t the model; it’s the grind. It's the hours spent on robotic work: hunting for leads, enriching contact data, manually updating the CRM, and sending endless follow-up emails. This is where reps burn out, and it plagues both inside and outside teams. AI is the solution. It automates the grunt work, freeing up humans to do what they do best: build relationships, think strategically, and close deals. At Topo, our philosophy is simple: let robots do the robotic work so humans can do the human work. Here’s how it works in practice. An AI SDR, like the ones powered by Topo, can monitor the entire market for buying signals, identify your ideal customers, find their correct contact information, and launch personalized, multi-channel outreach campaigns. It handles the first 10 touches that a human SDR would, but does it 24/7 with perfect consistency. When a lead is warm and ready for a real conversation, it hands it off to a human rep. Suddenly, your inside sales reps are only having high-quality conversations, and your outside sales reps can walk into meetings that are already pre-qualified and warmed up. Career Paths and Skills: What’s in It for You? If you're an AE scrolling through this on your phone, you're probably wondering what this all means for your career and your bank account. Let’s get pragmatic. Salary and Compensation Trends Historically, outside sales roles have offered higher base salaries and on-target earnings (OTE), largely because they handle bigger, more complex deals. However, the gap is narrowing. Top-performing inside sales reps at fast-growing tech companies can easily out-earn their field sales counterparts. Inside sales also often provides a faster, more structured path into sales leadership because the management and coaching model is more centralized. If you want to understand what OTE actually means for your paycheck, it's worth digging into the details. Don’t take our word for it. Check sites like RepVue or Glassdoor for real-time, role-specific compensation data in your industry and location. The Skills You'll Build in Each Role Neither path is “better”—they just build different muscles. Choosing a path is about deciding which skills you want to sharpen. Inside Sales builds : Tech-savviness, high-volume prospecting, process optimization, written and verbal conciseness, and exceptional time management. You become a master of efficiency. Outside Sales builds : In-person negotiation, C-level presentation skills, strategic account planning, autonomy, and the ability to read a room. You become a master of influence and strategy. The ultimate power move? Get experience in both. Or even better, join a modern hybrid team where you can flex both sets of skills. For a broader perspective on mapping your sales career, see Your Sales Career Path Isn't a Ladder . The debate over inside sales vs outside sales is a relic of a bygone era. It was a relevant question when your only tools were a telephone and a company car. Today, it’s a false choice. The winning formula isn't about where your reps sit; it's about the intelligence of the system they operate in. The future of sales belongs to teams that stop arguing about outdated models and start building a smarter engine—one that blends human creativity and strategic thinking with the relentless efficiency of AI automation.

FanDuel and FanDuel Sports Network continue broadening strategic partnership with launch of bet tracking across select NBA and NHL games
body_text: NEW YORK and SOUTHPORT, Conn. – Dec. 16, 2025 – FanDuel, the premier online gaming company in North America, and Main Street Sports Group, owner of FanDuel Sports Network, the largest holder of local sports media rights, today announced the launch of Bet Tracking, an interactive viewing feature that now allows fans in select markets to follow their FanDuel Sportsbook bets in real time while watching live NBA and NHL games on FanDuel Sports Network. Now live, in the markets where online sports betting is legal, the new integration marks another milestone in creating an interactive, participatory viewing experience for local fans. Over the past year, the strategic partnership between FanDuel and Main Street Sports Group has helped enhance the local sports viewing experience and deepen FanDuel’s presence in regional markets. Built on FanDuel Sports Network’s in-house technology platform and powered by FanDuel’s account-linking system, Bet Tracking bridges live game action with fans’ wagers, updating in real time as play unfolds. Bet Tracking has officially launched across select FanDuel Sports Network NBA broadcasts including the Cleveland Cavaliers, Charlotte Hornets, Detroit Pistons, Indiana Pacers, and Memphis Grizzlies, as well as NHL coverage of the Carolina Hurricanes, Columbus Blue Jackets, Detroit Red Wings, St. Louis Blues and Nashville Predators. The feature is available to fans in those markets by logging onto FanDuelSportsNetwork.com or the FanDuel Sports Network app using their direct-to-consumer (DTC) or pay-TV credentials, as well as Prime Video. Media assets including images and video related to Bet Tracking are available for download here . “ The integration of Bet Tracking into live NBA and NHL games on FanDuel Sports Network represents another significant milestone in our partnership and our commitment to delivering an unparalleled viewing experience to fans ,” said Mike Raffensperger, President of Sports, FanDuel . “ Over the past year, our partnership with FanDuel Sports Network has elevated our brand presence, deepened engagement across our products, and proven the impact of combining live local sports with interactive technology. We look forward to continuing this successful partnership and exploring new ways to collaborate in the future as we remain committed to driving innovation at the intersection of sports entertainment and betting .” In addition to bet tracking, the partnership has introduced additional fan-first experiences, including: Account linking capabilities , so fans can connect their FanDuel Sportsbook account directly to FanDuel Sports Network, enabling the Bet Tracking feature and making it simpler to toggle between the two offerings. Expanded on-screen odds integrations into nightly NBA and NHL broadcasts, giving viewers up-to-date information during the same markets and broadcasts where Bet Tracking is available. Broadened live content portfolio including shared premier live events rights such as EuroLeague Basketball and PDC Darts, plus syndicated content from The Ringer that provides betting insights powered by FanDuel odds. Exclusive offers including a “Bet $5, Get 3 Months on Us” promotion in which customers who place a $5 bet in FanDuel Sportsbook or enter any paid FanDuel daily fantasy contest will receive a trial subscription to FanDuel Sports Network’s DTC streaming service. Joint activation around Missouri’s Sportsbook launch featuring in-market events, on-air integrations and promotions, and elevated VIP experiences tied to the state’s legalization of online sports betting on December 1. “ In markets where FanDuel Sports Network and FanDuel’s Sportsbook operate together, we’re seeing meaningful, sustained growth ,” said Eric Ratchman, Chief Revenue Officer, Main Street Sports Group . “ Fans who engage with FanDuel’s on-screen integrations are watching nearly twice as many games per season and staying connected with our product more than 40 days longer on average. That level of engagement underscores the power of how this partnership is helping to shape the future of local sports viewing" . A Transformational Year of Growth and Innovation Since the partnership’s launch last fall, FanDuel and FanDuel Sports Network have introduced a series of fan-first experiences that have expanded access, elevated engagement, and deepened local market connections. Key accomplishments from the first year include: Rebranding 15 regional networks under the FanDuel Sports Network name, making FanDuel a household brand across millions of homes. Launching new in-game odds integrations with the Cincinnati Reds and Detroit Tigers. Shared commitments to promoting responsible gaming using FanDuel Sports Networks reach to encourage viewers to use FanDuel’s responsible gaming tools and highlight available support resources. Introducing exclusive offers for DTC subscribers. Expanding programming by simulcasting FanDuel TV’s Up & Adams and Run It Back on FanDuel Sports Network. For more information, please contact corporatemedia@flutter.com . Sign up to email alerts here .

U.S. Army Selects Dynamo AI to Advance Scalable AI Risk Management for Mission-Critical Defense Applications
summary: U.S. Army Selects Dynamo AI to Advance Scalable AI Risk Management for Mission-Critical Defense Applications
body_text: SBIR Direct to Phase II Award accelerates the deployment of trustworthy AI through advanced evaluation, observability, and risk mitigation solutions. Dynamo AI, a leading provider of test, evaluation, and custom guardrails, was awarded a U.S. Army SBIR contract focused on Scalable Tools for Automated AI Risk Management and Algorithmic Analysis for mission-critical defense applications. Through this Direct to Phase II contract, Dynamo AI will help set conditions for secure, scalable AI/ML integration to accelerate the deployment of advanced analytics and deliver trusted AI at speed and scale. Dynamo AI will develop tailored AI model evaluations to ensure system performance and trustworthiness, as well as guardrails customized to U.S. Army use cases, enabling real-time observability, security, and privacy. These capabilities will be reinforced with automated stress testing to identify risks such as data leakage, adversarial jailbreaking, and hallucination vulnerabilities, ensuring Army AI systems are robust, compliant, and mission-ready. “The Department of Defense is accelerating adoption of AI, but mission success depends on trust – the reliability, security, and accountability of these systems,” said Christian Lau, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at Dynamo AI. “Through this contract, Dynamo will equip the Army with scalable AI risk management capabilities that ensure AI systems can perform safely and effectively in the most demanding defense environments. ” At project completion, the Army will gain a ready-to-deploy, mission-aligned toolkit that enhances AI risk management, ultimately strengthening the security, reliability, and transparency of AI-enabled systems across critical defense operations. ‍ About Dynamo AI Dynamo AI is the trusted AI test, evaluation, guardrail, and observability platform for pioneers in financial services, insurance, and defense. With Dynamo AI, organizations gain real-time security and mission visibility into their AI applications, enabling assurance and accelerating deployments. ‍

title: Landstar Gives Back in 2025
summary: No matter the season, Landstar employees are dedicated to making a positive impact on their communities.
body_text: Giving Back, All Year Long No matter the season, Landstar employees are dedicated to making a positive impact on their communities. During 2025, employees across the country supported a wide range of causes and charitable organizations, helping generate thousands of dollars, hundreds of boxes of donations and countless hours of service toward making a difference for their neighbors in need. These companywide efforts are coordinated through Annette Hartley, Human Resources Employee Engagement & Intranet Administrator, who has been with Landstar for twenty years, and are supported by Sydney Larson, Human Resources Specialist. Second Helping Landstar likes to serve up twice the effort to help their communities combat food insecurity. In Rockford, Illinois, both current and retired employees dish out kindness year-round at Carpenter's Place, a nonprofit homeless day center. Every three months, the Rockford community has the opportunity to have a free lunch at the outreach facility, with Landstar organizing both fundraising events and food preparation. Thanks to their efforts, over 400 guests were fed a hot meal in 2025. Recently, the Jacksonville headquarters once again partnered with Feeding Northeast Florida to ensure a bountiful Thanksgiving for its community during its annual food drive. There was even more to be thankful for this year, especially due to the efforts of Debbie Templeton and Alexis Williams, the two employees who coordinated the drive. With Landstar's contributions, Feeding Northeast Florida was able to provide 22,998 more meals and collect 743lbs of food. In total, Landstar generated 23,618 meals on behalf of the nonprofit. On donation day, Feeding Northeast Florida visited the headquarters to load up overflowing boxes of packaged and canned goods. Santa's Helpers As the holiday season ramps up, so does the community outreach. For the past 35 years, generous employees at Landstar's Jacksonville headquarters have partnered with the Child Guidance Center (CGC), which offers support services to children and families in the area, to provide holiday gifts for at-risk youth. This year, employees donated over 120 new bikes and helmets, which Landstar helped deliver in time for the holidays. Employees also collected gifts and monetary donations for the Christmas wish lists of 125 children in need at CGC, thanks in part to Kristin McNaron, who coordinated the effort. Thanks to Rockford employees, the Winnebago/Boone County Foster Care Alliance Adopt-an-Angel program was able to grant 55 Christmas wish lists for foster children in their community. With the support of Lori Bauch, who coordinated the collection, children in the foster system received everything from toys to warm clothes this winter. Driving Change Throughout the year, employees participate in drives to keep the spirit of goodwill alive outside of the holiday season. School supply drives held in Jacksonville and Rockford collected hundreds of folders, notebooks, crayons, and backpacks for underprivileged students at Holiday Hill Elementary in Jacksonville and Riverdahl Elementary in Rockford. Coupled with ongoing blood drives in Jacksonville and Rockford, their donations provided enough blood to save over 300 lives and made a difference year-round. A Place to Call Home In the transportation industry, it's important to have a place to call home. With that in mind, Landstar recently teamed up with Habitat for Humanity, whose mission is to build and repair homes for families in need. Employees from the Rockford service center volunteered to help build a new home for a family in their community. Twenty employee volunteers supported the nonprofit's vision of a world where everyone has a decent, affordable place to live by taking a day out of the office to build a new single-family home. As the first home build of the partnership, the program will continue through 2026 at both the Jacksonville and Rockford locations. In addition, Landstar and its employees participated in the following corporate runs, raising funds and awareness: Relay For Life with the American Cancer Society in Jacksonville, Florida BKS Partners Corporate Run 5K in Jacksonville, Florida

title: Meeting the Demands of Next-Gen Client Computing with a High-Performance, High-Reliability SPD Hub
summary: As the world of client computing rapidly evolves, the demand for higher memory performance is at a premium. Gaming, AI, and other advanced applications
body_text: As the world of client computing rapidly evolves, the demand for higher memory performance is at a premium. Gaming, AI, and other advanced applications are pushing DDR5 data rates to 6400 MT/s and beyond. While these advancements unlock new possibilities, they also introduce new challenges for memory module makers, PC OEMs, and motherboard manufacturers. The High-Speed DDR5 Challenge With every leap in data rate, the electrical environment inside client systems becomes increasingly noisy. This is true for the I2C/I3C sideband bus, which is critical for module configuration and management. As noise levels rise, so do the risks of communication errors, reliability issues, and implementation headaches. Why Sideband Reliability Matters The I2C/I3C bus is the backbone of out-of-band communication for DDR5 modules. At high speeds, even minor disruptions can lead to costly troubleshooting and delays in bringing new products to market. Ensuring robust, reliable sideband communication is essential for delivering the performance and reliability end-users demand. Introducing the Rambus SPD Hub: Engineered for Reliability Rambus, a trusted supplier to leading DRAM manufacturers, has developed an SPD Hub with advanced filtering specifically designed to address the challenges of noisy, high-speed DDR5 environments. Key features include: Advanced serial interface filtering for exceptional noise immunity Integrated temperature sensor for real-time monitoring and enhanced reliability Expanded non-volatile memory for custom applications and robust data management The SPD Hub is part of a complete Rambus chipset for DDR5 CSODIMMs, CUDIMMs, and LPCAMM2 modules, including Client Clock Drivers and PMICs. This integrated approach simplifies purchasing, improves interoperability, and reduces total cost of ownership. Ready to Overcome DDR5 Implementation Challenges? If your team is facing increased noise, communication issues, or reliability concerns as you scale up DDR5 performance, you’re not alone. The Rambus SPD Hub is engineered to help you deliver the next generation of high-performance, reliable client computing solutions.
